body: ac-03 isolated corpus pass (2026-06-17, output/username-veto-gate/): same-binary baseline (veto-off) vs candidate (veto-on) over the 33k sample SUCCEEDED, but revealed the rule OVER-FIRES. Relocation full_name->username = 2217, of which 1209 (55%) were LOW-cardinality false positives (fullexchangename 562 [exchange codes NMS/NYQ], platform_name 120, generic_drug_name 92, dns_qry_rcode_name 64, role_name 62). FIX SHIPPED to main (unreleased): distinct-fraction >= 0.9 guard (commit c650120). RESIDUAL: even guarded, single-token HIGH-distinct name columns leak (state_name 58, api_name, column_name, country names) — the semantic ceiling (cardinality-boundary-error-is-real); value-only guards can't fully separate username from other single-token name types. TWO BLOCKERS before ship: (1) the corpus_honest_gate.py call FAILED (Binder Error: ydf_prediction_gated not found) — the isolated same-binary baseline pass wrote sense_prediction only; a proper run needs --fill-ydf + gating on BOTH passes so --baseline carries the oracle. Fix overnight_username_veto_gate.sh accordingly. (2) re-run gold (--reframe) with the guarded binary + isolate a same-binary gold baseline; the un-guarded run showed 0.797 with venue_country/id mislabelled to username (residual tail). DECISION NEEDED (morning): is the guarded rule's author-handle win worth its residual single-token-name FP tail, or is it too leaky to ship?
